cf.title: pg_ctl start may return 0 even if the postmaster has been already started on Windows

input.subject: pg_ctl start may return 0 even if the postmaster has been already started on Windows

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a or 1b: the bug is stated in message #1 and committers agree it should be fixed. The surviving objections are fixable level 2 points about the CreateProcess() design. prior-attempts-1 is the strongest, because message #34 reverted /D for the same user-visible effect. maintenance-fit-1 needs a committer who knows Windows token handling to sign.

brief.title: pg_ctl start on Windows reports success when a server already runs
brief.problem: On Windows, `pg_ctl start` can return 0 when the cluster was already started less than 2 seconds earlier. pg_ctl launches the postmaster through cmd.exe, so it knows only the shell PID and cannot check that postmaster.pid belongs to its own child. Scripts and tools such as pg_upgrade that rely on the exit code get a wrong result.
brief.proposed_design: The original patch keeps cmd.exe, adds /D to disable autorun, and walks the process table for a postgres.exe child of the launcher shell to get the real postmaster PID. Later messages offer two other designs: pg_ctl passes a random token that the postmaster writes to postmaster.pid, or pg_ctl starts postgres.exe directly with CreateProcess() and handle-based redirection. The latest patches follow the CreateProcess() design.
user_visible_surface: `pg_ctl start` on Windows returns failure when another postmaster already runs in the data directory.
`pg_ctl start` on Windows may print different error messages, consolidated to "could not start server".
The launcher cmd.exe runs with /D, so registry AutoRun commands no longer run (committed, then reverted for v17).
The token design would add a new value in postmaster.pid and a way for pg_ctl to pass it to the postmaster.
author_claims: Process table walking fixes the bug, and several reviewers report it passes CI.
Removing the short sleep in 001_start_stop.pl reproduces the bug, and the patch fixes it.
The CreateProcess() patch passes all Windows regression tests, including CI with elevated privileges.
CreateProcess() fixes the root cause with about 250 lines of Windows-only code and keeps privilege dropping.
The latest refinement passes LocalSystem, LocalService and elevated tests on x64 and ARM64 with paths that contain spaces and U+00E9.
brief.thread_state: Committers have not chosen among process table walking, the token, and CreateProcess(); Álvaro Herrera favors CreateProcess() for master and a smaller fix for back branches. The entry has moved through 13 CommitFests, and a new v6 patch from October 2026 has no reply.
unclear: The material does not say which design the current CommitFest patch implements or who maintains it.
The material does not say whether a fix goes to back branches, or which one.
Yasir Shah says the bug is absent in v16, and nobody confirms or refutes that.
The material does not say why the CreateProcess() patch waits 2 seconds to detect `postgres -C`, or whether that slows startup.
Harrison reports failing Unicode executable checks that also fail unpatched, and nobody explains them.
Two global PID variables in the v3 CreateProcess() patch need cleanup per Álvaro Herrera; the material does not say if v6 does this.

objections.title: Dropping cmd.exe brings back the AutoRun change reverted for v17
objections.failure_scenario: A Windows administrator sets a cmd.exe AutoRun entry, for example `chcp` or environment variables, that the postmaster inherits today through the launcher shell. After the CreateProcess() change, `pg_ctl start` runs postgres.exe directly, so the entry never runs. The administrator finds out only when server log encoding or environment differs after an upgrade.
objections.argument: Message #32 argued that it is not Postgres's job to second-guess the user's AutoRun settings, and that /D on only some %comspec% callers is inconsistent. Message #34 reverted /D for that reason. Running postgres.exe without cmd.exe has the same user-visible effect for pg_ctl start, while pgwin32_system() keeps running AutoRun. Messages #40-#43 do not discuss this.
objections.author_must_show: Why is skipping AutoRun acceptable for pg_ctl start under CreateProcess() when the same effect from /D was reverted, and what happens to other %comspec% callers?

critic.reasoning: Message #32 objected to skipping AutoRun in only some callers, and message #34 reverted /D on that basis. Direct launch has the same effect for pg_ctl start, and messages #40-#43 do not address it.

objections.title: Second copy of the privilege-dropping logic for the postmaster launch
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch changes which groups or privileges CreateRestrictedProcess() removes, for example after a Windows change. The new CreateProcessAsUser() path in start_postmaster() keeps the old token rules. An elevated pg_ctl then starts a postmaster with more rights than intended, and nothing in CI reports the difference.
objections.argument: Message #40 says the new code builds its own restricted token, "matching the behavior of the existing CreateRestrictedProcess() function". Matching by copy means two places must stay in sync, and only elevated-privilege tests would show a gap. Message #43 adds a refinement that opens log files under the restricted identity, so this security-sensitive code grows further. The prose does not say whether v6 shares one helper with CreateRestrictedProcess().
objections.author_must_show: Does the direct launch reuse the same token-building code as CreateRestrictedProcess(), so one change covers both paths?

critic.reasoning: Message #40 says the new path builds a restricted token that matches CreateRestrictedProcess(). Neither the thread nor the patch prose says the two paths share code, so the risk that they drift apart stands.

objections.title: pg_ctl -o and -l lose cmd.exe parsing without a stated contract
objections.failure_scenario: A Windows service is registered with pg_ctl register -o containing %PGDATA2% or caret-escaped quotes, and the stored command line is expanded by cmd.exe at each start. After the change, CreateProcess() passes the string literally and the postmaster rejects the option or reads the wrong path. The user finds out at the next service restart.
objections.argument: Today start_postmaster() builds a cmd.exe command line, so -o text and the -l redirection go through cmd.exe quoting, %VAR% expansion and append semantics. Message #40 describes handle-based redirection, but not whether -o text is parsed the same way or whether the log file is still appended to. Message #43 tests paths with spaces and U+00E9, but not shell metacharacters or variables in -o.
objections.author_must_show: Is the postmaster command line, including -o text with %VAR%, ^ and quotes, and the -l append behaviour, identical with and without cmd.exe, and is any difference documented?

critic.reasoning: pg_ctl start passes -o text and the `>>` log redirection through cmd.exe today, and messages #40 and #43 do not say that parsing and append behaviour stay the same. The service scenario is weak support: as far as I know, service start already launches postgres.exe without cmd.exe.

objections.title: Fixed 2-second wait to detect postgres -C
objections.failure_scenario: On a loaded Windows CI machine, a postgres -C child or an early-failing postmaster takes longer than 2 seconds to exit. pg_ctl takes the wrong branch and the test fails only sometimes. Developers then find intermittent failures that look like unrelated Windows noise.
objections.argument: Message #40 says the direct launch waits 2 seconds when there is no log file, to tell postgres -C apart from server startup. That puts a new timing threshold into code whose main fault is already a 2-second clock allowance (message #1). Timing thresholds tend to need retuning, and the material does not say whether v6 keeps this wait or replaces it with an exit-status check.
objections.author_must_show: Can the launch tell postgres -C from server startup without a fixed delay, and does v6 still contain the 2-second wait?

critic.reasoning: Message #40 states a fixed 2-second wait to tell `postgres -C` from server startup, and no later message says v6 removes it. A slow exit on a loaded machine would take the wrong branch.

refuted.title: Direct CreateProcess() launch drops cmd.exe AutoRun, the change reverted for v17
refuted.failure_scenario: An administrator sets a Command Processor AutoRun entry that runs chcp, sets environment variables or maps a drive for the postmaster. After the upgrade, pg_ctl starts postgres.exe without cmd.exe, so the server starts with a different code page or environment. The administrator finds out when log encoding or tablespace paths stop working.
refuted.argument: In message #32 Noah Misch argued that AutoRun is not Postgres's to second-guess, and message #34 reverted the /D change down to 17 on that basis. Removing cmd.exe entirely has the same user-visible effect, but messages #40 and #43 do not mention AutoRun. Message #42 plans different launch mechanisms on master and back branches, so users would see this difference between major versions.
refuted.author_must_show: Why is dropping AutoRun now acceptable when /D was reverted for that reason, and what will the release notes tell users who rely on it?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of prior-attempts-1, which states the same AutoRun point and also covers the inconsistency with pgwin32_system().

refuted.title: Direct launch adds a second privilege-dropping path for the postmaster
refuted.failure_scenario: An administrator runs pg_ctl start from an elevated prompt or a LocalSystem service. If the new CreateProcessAsUser() path drops a different set of groups or privileges than CreateRestrictedProcess(), the postmaster keeps Administrator rights, and SQL-level code paths that reach the file system then run with them. Nobody finds out until someone inspects the process token.
refuted.argument: Message #40 says the new code builds its own restricted token and only claims to match CreateRestrictedProcess(). The material does not say whether it shares that code. Message #43 changes which identity opens the log file, so the drop logic has already changed between versions without a review that compared it to the existing function. Message #38 notes that the reviewers are not Windows experts, so a mistake here may go unnoticed.
refuted.author_must_show: Does the direct-launch path reuse CreateRestrictedProcess() token logic, and which test shows that an elevated pg_ctl start gives the postmaster the same token as today?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-1. Its own scenario depends on an unshown difference between the two token paths, and message #43 reports passing LocalSystem, LocalService and elevated tests.

refuted.title: Different Windows launch mechanisms on master and back branches
refuted.failure_scenario: Master ships CreateProcess() and the back branches ship process-table walking, as message #42 suggests. A later Windows bug in pg_ctl start then needs two unrelated fixes for about five years. Whoever backpatches finds that the master fix does not apply and must work out the older path again.
refuted.argument: Message #42 favors CreateProcess() for master and "perhaps Kyotaro's earlier version" for back branches. The process-table walk depends on a check against an extra cmd.exe child that message #25 says appears "for unknown reasons". Each branch would keep Windows-only code that only a few people can reason about. The thread has not decided whether back branches get any fix, and message #36 says the bug may not exist in v16.
refuted.author_must_show: Which branches does the fix target, and if they differ, why is a second launch mechanism in back branches worth its upkeep compared with leaving them unfixed?

critic.reasoning: Message #42 only suggests the split with "perhaps"; no patch proposes it. A smaller fix in back branches than on master is existing Postgres practice, and the scenario describes a normal backpatching cost.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: The token design would add a value to postmaster.pid, and pg_upgrade relies on the pg_ctl start exit code.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: The CreateProcess() design builds its own restricted token to drop privileges for the postmaster.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: It is a bug fix, the /D change was reverted for v17, and message #42 suggests a smaller fix for back branches.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: About 250 lines of Windows-only launch and token code in pg_ctl.c that few reviewers can check.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Why is skipping cmd.exe AutoRun acceptable under CreateProcess() when message #34 reverted /D for the same effect, and what happens to other %comspec% callers?
Does the direct launch share the token-building code with CreateRestrictedProcess(), so one change covers both paths?
Are -o text with %VAR%, ^ and quotes, and the -l append behaviour, the same with and without cmd.exe?
Does v6 still wait 2 seconds to detect postgres -C, and can the launch tell the two cases apart without a fixed delay?
Which branches does the fix target, and does the bug exist in v16 as message #36 questions?

committability.owner_note: Álvaro Herrera states a design preference in message #42; the owner needs to know Windows process creation and restricted tokens, and message #38 notes that reviewers are not Windows experts.
committability.liability: The owner signs for Windows-only launch and privilege-dropping code in pg_ctl for as long as Windows is supported, and for any behaviour change seen by AutoRun or -o users.
committability.author_follow_up: A v6 patch arrived in October 2026 and has no reply; the entry is Waiting on Author, and the material does not say who maintains the current patch.

priority.reason: The bug affects Windows scripts and tools that trust the pg_ctl start exit code, with CI flakiness as the only shown impact. The entry has moved through 13 CommitFests without a design decision, and v6 needs a committer who knows Windows to review it.

provisional_note: Without the code, nobody can tell whether v6 shares token code with CreateRestrictedProcess(), keeps the 2-second wait, or cleans up the two global PID variables. The Unicode executable check failures that Harrison reports are also unexplained.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Let pg_ctl check the result of a postmaster config reload
precedents_retrieved.summary: The postmaster records the time and success of its last config file load attempt in a new line of postmaster.pid. After sending the reload signal, pg_ctl reload waits for that line to change and reports whether the reload succeeded.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding after review, and the entry was returned with feedback after a month with no update. Heikki Linnakangas asked for a counter instead of a one-second timestamp, which fails for two reloads in the same second or when the clock moves backwards. He also asked for a clearer return convention for ProcessConfigFileInternal, a smaller pidfile parser, and documentation. Tom Lane had earlier objected to that return convention and suggested views for pg_hba.conf and pg_ident.conf, and the author left it to him whether to continue.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch had feedback, but there has been no update in the last
month, so I am now marking it as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Create a new session for postmaster in pg_ctl
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch made the postmaster call setsid() so it leaves the controlling terminal's session, which stops a Ctrl-C in the starting shell from killing the server. After Tom Lane's review, the author moved the setsid() call into pg_ctl start.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier objected that the pg_ctl version breaks a development workflow: Ctrl-C on pg_ctl during recovery no longer stops the started instance. He asked for an opt-in switch with the current behavior as default, while Tom Lane preferred detaching by default and suggested a postmaster switch that pg_ctl passes. Andres Freund opposed the postmaster daemonizing itself, and the patch was returned with feedback for an optional pg_ctl-based approach.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I would be ready to
accept a patch which does not change the default behavior, and makes the
deamonization behavior activated only if an option switch is given by
the user, like -d/--daemon.  So I am -1 for what is proposed in its
current shape.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve logrotate test so that it meaningfully exercises syslogger.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Improve logrotate test so that it meaningfully exercises syslogger.
Reverted commit(s): Don't do pg_ctl logrotate test on Windows
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Discussion of bug #15804 reveals that this test didn't really prove
that the syslogger child process ever launched successfully, much
less did anything.  It was only checking that the expected log file
gets created, and that's done in the postmaster.  Moreover, the
test assumed it could rename the log file, which is likely to fail
on Windows (cf. commit d611175e5).

Instead, use the default log file name pattern, which should result
in a new file name being chosen after 1 second, and verify that
rotation has occurred by checking for a new file name.  Also add code
to test that messages actually do propagate through the syslogger.

In theory this version of the test should work on Windows, so
revert d611175e5.

Revert commits 290acac92b and 8a7e9e9dad.

precedents_retrieved.objection:
This commit revert the commits to add a test case that tests the 'force'
option when there is an active backend connected to the database being
dropped.

This feature internally sends SIGTERM to all the backends connected to the
database being dropped and then the same is reported to the client.  We
found that on Windows, the client end of the socket is not able to read
the data once we close the socket in the server which leads to loss of
error message which is not what we expect.  We also observed  similar
behavior in other cases like pg_terminate_backend(),
pg_ctl kill TERM <pid>.  There are probably a few others like that.  The
fix for this requires further study.

precedents_retrieved.title: Avoid possibly slow processing during postmaster abnormal or immediate shutdown
precedents_retrieved.summary: Two patches to shorten postmaster shutdown after a backend crash or an immediate shutdown. One makes the stats collector exit on SIGQUIT without writing the stats files, and the other closes the listening sockets as soon as the postmaster knows it will stop all children and exit.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane argued that commit 82233ce7e in 9.4 already solves the problem better, because the postmaster now sends SIGKILL to child processes after 5 seconds during a crash or immediate shutdown. The original complaint was against 9.2. Peter Eisentraut agreed, and he also objected that early socket close stops PQping() and error-message monitoring and makes the crash and immediate modes behave differently from the other shutdown modes.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
My feeling is that 82233ce7e has obsoleted all of the proposals made so
far in this thread, and that we should reject them all.

precedents_retrieved.title: Start WAL streaming as early as possible, without waiting for startup process to finish replaying existing WAL. This helps synchronous replication to resume quickly when significant replay lag has been built up.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch starts the WAL receiver on a standby before the startup process finishes replaying WAL already in pg_wal, so synchronous commits on the primary are not held up by replay lag. A GUC, wal_receiver_start_condition, picks when the receiver starts, and the start LSN is the beginning of the most recently flushed segment, found by reading the first page of each segment in pg_wal.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier objected that the start LSN is roughly the consistency point, so streaming begins too early when many local segments, often copied by hand, are still left to replay. He also rejected the WAL page checks as hard to maintain, noted that the patch requests streaming when PrimaryConnInfo is not set, and suggested a WAL reader scan from the redo point to find the real end of local WAL. The entry stayed "Waiting on Author" after this review and was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Your patch would cause streaming to begin too early, and a manual copy of segments is not a rare thing as in some environments a bulk copy of segments can make the catchup of a standby faster than streaming.

(via --outputdir) from pg_regress to the MSVC script vcregress.pl, as

for the sake of not breaking again the behavior we expect on Windows.

Thanks to Thomas Munro and Andrew Dunstan for the discussion.

precedents_retrieved.title: Teach autovacuum.c to launch workers to advance table age without attendant antiwraparound cancellation behavior
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch separates the rule that an antiwraparound autovacuum cannot be auto-cancelled from the XID age that launches it, so table-age autovacuums stay cancellable until a later age. In v5 a new setting, autovacuum_no_auto_cancel_age, sets that later age (default 1.8x the launch threshold), and a first patch adds instrumentation for what triggered each autovacuum.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Geoghegan withdrew the entry, saying he could not do more work on it. He did not give a reason beyond that. Before that, Robert Haas objected that keeping these autovacuums cancellable could make things worse for users whose autovacuums are already cancelled repeatedly. He found the evidence too speculative to justify the change, and the thread did not resolve this. Andres Freund was still asking for changes to the structure and naming of the instrumentation patch (0001).
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: In my opinion, this is too speculative to justify making changes to the behavior.

precedents_retrieved.title: Changing the autovacuum launcher scheduling; oldest table first algorithm
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes how the autovacuum launcher picks a database when one is at risk of wraparound, so that it picks the database holding the oldest table in the cluster. Running autovacuum workers advertise in shared memory the datfrozenxid that each database will have after their work, and the launcher uses this to choose.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stopped applying, and the author did not rebase it after Michael Paquier asked for one. Few reviewers took it up, and the author agreed the design needs to be reconsidered after the discussion. That discussion included Alvaro Herrera's older prioritisation patch and the author's later idea that workers report their progress to the launcher.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I would have suggested to mark the patch as returned with feedback
instead as the thing does not apply for some time now, and the author
has been notified about a rebase.

precedents_retrieved.title: reduce impact of lengthy startup and checkpoint tasks
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set adds a new auxiliary process, the custodian, that takes slow O(n) cleanup work out of startup and checkpoints. Later versions move removal of old serialized logical decoding snapshots and logical rewrite mapping files to it, with temporary file cleanup planned for a follow-up thread.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected again to moving snapshot and mapping file removal to the custodian, because without further work this raises the wraparound risk tied to the file names. Tom Lane said there was little point in going ahead without the RemovePgTempFiles task, which had been dropped from the patch set, and asked whether a long-lived custodian is the right model at all. The author planned a reworked version for the July commitfest but had none ready when asked.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Hmm, given Andres' objections there's little point in moving forward without that task.

precedents_retrieved.title: ALTER TABLE - check for column existence before starting operations
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a check in the first (preparation) pass of ALTER TABLE so that a column referenced by a subcommand such as SET NOT NULL is verified to exist, or to be added by another subcommand, before any expensive work like building a primary key starts. The goal is to fail fast on typos instead of holding a long lock and generating WAL that is then discarded.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The only review raised a memory-release issue (the heap tuple not being freed) and a behavioural regression: because subcommands run in passes by type, a command that alters a column and adds the same column later in the list used to succeed and fails with the patch, which could break backward compatibility. The visible messages show no revised patch or author reply after that review, and the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm not sure how important it is. But I think it could break backward
compatibility.

roaster_notes.note: No listed precedent matches. [P1] adds a postmaster.pid line, but its timestamp concern does not apply to a random token; [P5] and [P23] concern other pg_ctl behaviour. The only prior rejection found is inside this thread: /D was committed, then reverted (messages #21-#34).
Two objections from the standards and compatibility angle. Reporting failure when a server already runs fixes a bug and is not a compatibility objection.

The CreateProcess() design changes only how pg_ctl launches postgres.exe on Windows; it adds no WAL, catalog, on-disk, protocol or extension API state. Only the token design, which the latest patches do not follow, would add a postmaster.pid line, so this angle has nothing to object to.
The bug itself has no privilege aspect. Only the CreateProcess() design touches security, through its own token restriction.
The goal is a real bug fix that a committer supports in principle (messages #2, #42), so no objection is raised at levels 1a or 1b.

No existing feature, option or extension gives a correct `pg_ctl start` exit code on Windows, and checking `pg_ctl status` first is still racy. A possible overlap between the CreateProcess() launcher and the existing CreateRestrictedProcess() cannot be judged without the code.

This is a correctness bug, not a feature: `pg_ctl start` on Windows can return 0 when it did not start the server. Michael Paquier (message #2), Robert Haas (message #38) and Álvaro Herrera (message #42) agree it should be fixed, so there is no demand case to make against it. The only evidence of impact is CI flakiness in pg_upgrade tests (message #1), with no field reports. That bears on how large a rewrite is justified, which is a design question for other angles.
